evidence.shipped: articulated clearly enough that builders can act on it

findings.authorizedBy: House copy style, and catalog 4.21 read onto cleanly.
findings.diagnosis: The pass made the same substitution in On the Form, where the baseline reads articulated cleanly enough that they can evaluate it. The two sentences are a matched pair across the chapter, and cleanly is the exact word in both because the chapter's argument about form is that the apparatus of scholarship clutters an argument a builder needs uncluttered. Clearly is about comprehensibility, which the book never doubted. R-REGISTER-DICTION's test is equal precision, and here the volume's own word is the more precise of the two.

findings.summary: A three-part apposition describing the conversation was collapsed into a single relative clause.

evidence.baseline: an invitation into a larger conversation that is already underway, distributed across many traditions and communities, often without those traditions and communities recognizing each other
evidence.shipped: an invitation into a larger conversation already underway across many traditions and communities that often do not recognize one another

findings.authorizedBy: Catalog 4.8, redundant restatement, read onto the repeated traditions and communities.
findings.diagnosis: Three separate facts arrive in three separate movements: the conversation is underway, it is distributed, and its participants do not recognize each other. Compressed into one clause they become one fact with two modifiers, and the repetition of those traditions and communities, which the pass read as redundancy, is what makes the third movement land on the same nouns the second introduced. That is Chapter Eleven's entire argument restated in the book's final structural sentence, and the recognition it names is between the traditions rather than a property of them.

findings.summary: Three possessives and one relative construction were removed from the closing paragraph.

evidence.baseline: The argument the book makes will be tested ... The intellectual lineages it stands within will continue ... in whatever form their conditions permit
evidence.shipped: The argument will be tested ... The intellectual lineages in which it stands will continue ... in whatever form conditions permit

findings.diagnosis: Their conditions is the one that matters. The work belongs to whoever does it, in whatever form their conditions permit is the book's most complete grant of autonomy, and their is what makes the conditions the reader's own rather than the conditions the book has been describing. Without it the sentence permits whatever the general situation allows, which is a different and smaller freedom. The argument the book makes also distinguishes the argument from the book, which the section needs, since the next sentence says the lineages will continue regardless of what the project becomes.

regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. At four percent this was the least damaged section in the batch and it still lost the word its own chapter argued for. Cleanly appears twice in Chapter Thirteen, in the section defending the book's form and in the section defining what the book is, and the pass replaced it with clearly in both. Neither substitution is wrong in its sentence. Together they retire a term the chapter is about, which is the same volume-level effect recorded for each other in Chapter Eleven, produced the same way, by a copy-style preference applied consistently.
